_what: Layer-0 EVIDENCE record for data-gate (b). It asserts NO gamma and NO emergent number. It documents, against the PRIMARY developmental-neuroscience literature (cited), why each of the three brain regions still outside the M9 brain_organ_atlas (amygdala, septum, preoptic area) is kept at status tbd_master. The point is to upgrade these entries from an UN-examined 'tbd' to an EXAMINED, evidence-grounded 'genuinely ambiguous -> kept open per no-over-claim'. Forcing a single canonical master where the canon does not provide one would be exactly the over-claim the VP-SPEC no-tuning rule forbids. This file is read by NO engine function (it is documentation only); the frozen emergence tree is byte-unchanged by its presence.
_governance: VP-SPEC: gamma becomes Layer-1 [F measured] only when a region has ONE unambiguous canonical developmental master TF whose promoter can be fetched verbatim by the read-only eutils + SantaLucia-1998 NN dG37 pipeline (or cited verbatim from neuro v1.10.1). A region whose canon names several non-redundant masters, or whose single candidate master is SHARED with a region already in the atlas (double-counting the same promoter), does NOT meet that bar and is kept open. medium_efficacy_tested stays 0.0 (functional use OPEN regardless of region count).
_method: For each region: (1) state the question 'is there ONE canonical developmental master TF?'; (2) record what the primary literature actually shows; (3) give the no-over-claim verdict; (4) state precisely what external input would be required to ever close it. Sources are summarised in our own words with locator IDs; no source text is reproduced.
_relation_to_atlas: The 12 regions already in brain_organ_atlas.json are exactly the major brain regions/organs that DO have an unambiguous single canonical master (each gamma fetched or cited verbatim). The three regions below are exactly those that do NOT. Under the one-measured-master-per-region discipline, the atlas is therefore already SATURATED at the set of single-master-tractable regions: see completeness_statement.

regions.verdict: KEEP OPEN. The amygdala is not a developmental unit but a complex of nuclei with multiple, distinct embryonic origins; the literature names several non-redundant masters, not one. Forcing any single TF (OTP, LHX6, ISL1, PAX6, DLX5, ...) would mis-describe the biology and over-claim.
what_the_literature_shows: Central amygdala is itself split by origin: CeM principal cells are ISL1+ from the ventral LGE; CeC/CeL cells are PAX6+ from the dorsal LGE; the CeA at large carries the striatal marker DLX5 and lacks pallial markers (Frontiers Mol Neurosci 2024, central-amygdala diversity review).

Medial amygdala is multi-origin: subdivisions express different LIM genes (MeA-Lhx5, MePD-Lhx6, MePV-Lhx9; Choi 2005), it receives OTP+/SIM1+ glutamatergic neurons born in the lateral hypothalamic / telencephalo-hypothalamic (TOH) neuroepithelium (Medina lab, Front Neuroanat 2022; Morales 2021), DBX1- and FOXP2-marked inhibitory progenitors from the preoptic niche (Lischinsky et al., eLife 2017), and an EBF3+ glutamatergic population from a caudo-ventral pallial domain (Garcia-Moreno et al., 2018).
Basolateral/lateral amygdala principal neurons are pallial: DBX1+ and EMX1+ from lateral/basal pallium (Puelles tetrapartite model; Front Mol Neurosci 2024).
regions.why_not_resolved: No single one of these is THE amygdala master; each marks a different origin/subpopulation. This is a textbook case of developmental heterogeneity. Selecting one to obtain a gamma would be cherry-picking, not measurement.
regions.external_input_required_to_close: Either (i) future field consensus that the amygdala has a single canonical master (not expected; the consensus is the opposite), or (ii) a deliberate modeling change to a SUBNUCLEUS-level atlas where each subnucleus has its own single master (a different granularity than the organ-level atlas, out of current scope). Neither is available now.

regions.verdict: KEEP OPEN. The septum is marked by the ZIC family (ZIC1-5), but they act with strongly OVERLAPPING, partly REDUNDANT expression and are NOT septum-specific (the same Zic pattern marks thalamus, preoptic area, cortical hem and retina). No single Zic is established as THE septal master in the FOXG1/EN1 sense. Forcing 'ZIC1' would over-claim a specificity the canon does not support.
what_the_literature_shows: ZIC1, ZIC2, ZIC3 are co-expressed across the medial telencephalon including the septum from ~E12.5; ZIC4 is the most septum-enriched at later stages but is not characterised as a developmental master (Zic-family review, PMC11113920; Aruga/Nagai expression studies).

Zic1 and Zic3 are functionally redundant in expanding medial-forebrain progenitors; septal/olfactory-bulb hypoplasia is only partial and overlaps the Zic2 phenotype (Inoue et al., J Neurosci 2007, PMC6672357).

ZIC2 is principally a dorsal-midline / roof-plate / holoprosencephaly gene (the only gene linked to both classical and middle-interhemispheric HPE), i.e. broadly a midline patterning factor rather than a septum master (ZIC2-HPE literature).
Reviews state explicitly that assigning roles to individual Zic genes is complicated by overlapping expression and high sequence conservation within the family (Merzdorf, Dev Dyn 2007).
regions.why_not_resolved: Family redundancy + lack of septum specificity. A single-gene gamma would not represent 'the septal master' because no single gene plays that role unambiguously.
regions.external_input_required_to_close: Field consensus designating one canonical, septum-specific master TF (e.g. a loss-of-function study isolating a single non-redundant master). Not available; current evidence points to redundancy.

sources.topic: ZIC family review: overlapping Zic1-4 expression incl. septum; Zic4 septum-enriched
Zic1/Zic3 redundancy in medial forebrain; partial septum/OB hypoplasia
individual Zic roles confounded by overlap + sequence conservation
ZIC2 as dorsal-midline/HPE factor, not a septum-specific master

regions.verdict: KEEP OUT as an INDEPENDENT region (resolved, not merely tbd). The POA sits in the NKX2-1+ domain, but NKX2-1 is already the measured master of pallidum (gamma 1.5088) and is shared with hypothalamus; a POA entry would re-use the SAME NKX2-1 promoter measurement, double-counting one number as if it were an independent region. Additionally the POA is itself an internally parcellated progenitor niche (DBX1, FOXP2, SHH, NKX6.2 lineages), so it has no single distinct master of its own. The honest treatment is to recognise it as sharing NKX2-1 with regions already present (effectively folded), NOT to inflate the region count.
what_the_literature_shows: The POA is within the NKX2-1 expression domain together with the MGE, pallidum and hypothalamus (subpallial Nkx2-1 territory; Flames/Marin subpallial codes, J Neurosci 2007, 9682).

The POA neuroepithelium is heterogeneous: complementary DBX1+ and FOXP2+ progenitor pools, distinct from SHH and NKX6.2 lineages, that predict distinct postnatal (e.g. MeA) neuronal identities (Lischinsky et al., eLife 2017, PMC5384829).
regions.why_not_resolved: Its single candidate master is non-independent (already measured for pallidum) and the region is internally parcellated. Adding it would either double-count NKX2-1 or require an arbitrary distinct promoter target.
regions.external_input_required_to_close: A demonstrated POA-specific canonical master with its OWN distinct promoter (not NKX2-1 shared with pallidum/hypothalamus). Not available.

sources.topic: subpallial progenitor codes; POA in the Nkx2-1 domain

completeness_statement.claim: Under the one-measured-master-per-region discipline, brain_organ_atlas.json is SATURATED at the set of major brain regions that possess an unambiguous single canonical developmental master. The 12 included regions are exactly that set; the three excluded regions (amygdala, septum, POA) are excluded for a PRINCIPLED biological reason (no single non-redundant, non-shared master), not for lack of effort.
completeness_statement.consequence: Region count cannot be honestly increased at the organ level without one of: (a) future biological consensus naming a single master for a currently-heterogeneous region (external), or (b) a deliberate change of modeling granularity to subnuclei (a different atlas, out of current scope). Neither adds a tuned constant; both require inputs not now available.
completeness_statement.non_tuning_note: This is the no-tuning rule working as intended: the atlas grows only as fast as MEASURED, unambiguous masters become available, and stops exactly where the canon becomes ambiguous. The boundary is set by the biology, not by a target region count.
